item.title: Building a Local BIM-MEP Planning Tool
item.description:
My broader renovation approach covers things like decisions, costs, companies, documents, and generally trying to keep the renovation organised.

While working on that, I kept coming back to a different problem.

Once the house is finished, a lot of the important technical work will disappear. Cables will be inside walls, pipes under floors, ducts above ceilings, sensors mounted in places I will eventually forget about. Photos help, drawings help, but I wanted something I could actually inspect and search later.

item.title: Building the OLIMAT Treviso Website
item.description:
I was asked to build a website for OLIMAT Treviso, the Treviso district of the Italian Math Olympiad.

It was a project I was happy to work on for reasons that go a little beyond building the website itself. I participated in math competitions when I was in high school, and the Liceo Scientifico Leonardo da Vinci (my former high school) is also the school referenced by the project as the hub for the Treviso district.

item.title: Renovating My Grandfather’s House
item.description:
Renovating my grandfather’s house is a family project, but there is also quite a lot to keep track of. There are the usual questions about rooms, furniture and materials, but also quotations, companies, documents, payments, incentives and decisions that depend on each other.

Since I work on software projects, my instinct is to organise some of this information instead of keeping it across messages, folders and a few unrelated spreadsheets. I’m not trying to manage the renovation as if it were a software project, but some of the same habits are useful: keeping track of the current situation, writing down requirements, recording decisions and knowing which information belongs together.

item.title: Building a Private Home-Server Infrastructure
item.description:
I recently bought a mini-PC to use as a home server.

I have been wanting to move more of the software I use regularly onto my own hardware, but until now most of my self-hosting work has been made up of separate experiments. With this machine I want to put those services in one place and maintain them as part of the same system.

The server will run Debian and will only be remotely accessible through a VPN. Larger files and application data will be stored on directly attached storage, with separate encrypted backups.

item.title: Academic Projects at SJTU
item.description:
During my exchange period at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, I completed several coursework projects in materials science. Unlike the lecture notes shown here, these are self-contained studies developed within specific course contexts, specifically with a stronger emphasis on modelling, analysis, or literature review.

The documents below are shared as originally submitted, with only minor adjustments where necessary.

Projects

Modelling the Melting Behaviour of Pure Ni, Zr, and Ni-Zr Alloys

A molecular dynamics study (LAMMPS) of melting and phase transitions in pure Ni, Zr, and Ni-Zr intermetallics, with focus on atomistic-scale thermal behaviour.

item.title: LaTeX Notes for Politecnico di Milano
item.description:
I started using LaTeX in 2020 during my studies at Politecnico di Milano, and it has since become my main tool for academic writing. My current setup is based on Visual Studio Code with a small set of extensions and a growing collection of custom commands and snippets tailored to my workflow.

The material below is a curated selection of lecture notes and projects, highlighting examples of my typesetting and academic work rather than complete documents. Full documents are not publicly distributed; excerpts are shared for documentation purposes only.
